_comment: Edit this file to set your searches. Each search needs either a pasted Autotrader motorhome-search URL or a criteria block. See README.md for every supported key.

details._comment: Each new advert's page is fetched once to read its features and description. maxFetchesPerRun caps how many per run; delayMs is the pause between requests; adverts whose page says fewer berths than excludeIfBerthBelow are treated as unconverted vans and hidden. refetchTruncated re-reads adverts stored with a cut-short description (up to maxRefetchesPerRun a run) so kit mentioned late in a long blurb is not missed.

deals._comment: wantedSpecs is the star spec: the kit you most want, matched against each advert's page. Every advert is scored out of this list (shown as stars on the dashboard and in notifications). niceToHave is the second tier: each counts one point in the kit score against three per star item. Every advert also gets a pick score out of 100 (star spec 35, nice-to-have 10, price against similar 20, seller motivation 15, provenance 10, quality per pound 10, minus 25 per red flag); topPickScore is the bar for the dashboard Top picks view (45 is roughly the top 1% of the market). staleNoCutDays flags adverts listed that long with no price cut yet, once the job has watched them for staleNoCutWatchDays (earlier cuts are invisible to it). An advert is 'worth a look' if it has at least minWantedSpecs of them, or its price net of kit is underpricedPercent below similar live adverts, or its desperation score (0-100: price cuts seen up to 60, time listed up to 30, private seller 10) reaches dealScore. A seller counts as motivated at motivatedScore, but only with evidence: a price cut, or a private seller listed longer than staleDays. Any red flag removes it from the list. Labels must match the spec list in src/spec.js (or a top-level 'specs' override).

brief._comment: Your buyer's brief. 'Worth a look' now means an advert meets every must-have here and has no red flags; price and seller signals then rank it (pick score +15). Missing exactly one must-have makes it a 'near miss' (+5). heating: any one of these labels counts (Alde wet heating, modern diesel heating such as Truma Combi D, or underfloor heating); plain gas blown-air does not. avoidBrands: makes with the weakest owner-satisfaction scores in the Caravan and Motorhome Club surveys (weighted, 2020 to 2025: Elddis 74.6%, Chausson 75.0%, Swift 77.1%, Auto-Trail 77.1%, Pilote 77.5%, Bailey 77.7%) plus their sub-brands (Bessacarr, Ace, Compass, Joa and so on); they never count as worth a look and lose 15 pick points. bonus: nice extras, +3 each. A-class motorhomes are allowed. brandTiers: only makes rated premium or upper build in src/quality.js count (Hymer, Carthago, Niesmann+Bischoff, Frankia, Le Voyageur, Rapido, Morelo; Laika, Bürstner, Dethleffs, Knaus, Adria, Westfalia, VW California, Eura Mobil, Mega Mobil, IH). Volume British makes, value brands such as Benimar, Roller Team and McLouis, and budget sub-brands (Sun Living, Carado, Malibu...) are treated like the avoid list.

searches.name: Campervans and van conversions (length from advert)
All motorhomes (star spec research)
searches._comment: Every motorhome, campervan and van conversion on Autotrader in the price and year band, any length or body type, so the star spec can be scored across the whole market. The length rule below only flags these (dashboard toggle), it does not hide them.

length._comment: Overall length in metres. Worked out from Autotrader's spec sheet, a figure stated in the advert, or the base vehicle and wheelbase code (e.g. Ducato L4 = 6.36 m). mode 'hide' takes adverts outside the range off the dashboard (they stay under Hidden by rules); mode 'flag' keeps them all in and gives the dashboard a 'My length only' toggle instead. hideUnknown treats adverts whose length cannot be worked out as outside the range.
